Forecast Discussion

I’ll publish an Insights post today with a full rundown of weekend rain totals from Isaias.

The remnant low of Isaias has exited the Mid-Atlantic coast. Between it and high pressure to our southwest, we sit in a gusty northwest flow today. Low clouds with light rain or drizzle, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians, give way to clearing skies this afternoon as drier air arrives. The wind eases through the day.

The high builds over us Tuesday and Wednesday. Light wind and full sun push temperatures to near-record highs by Wednesday.

A front approaches Wednesday night and stalls to our north Thursday. We stay on its warm side--warm, but short of records. I cannot rule out a stray afternoon shower with the front that close.

A stronger cold front crosses Friday afternoon into evening with widely scattered showers, mostly on the west side. Cooler air arrives Friday night on a strong northwest wind.

Saturday is much cooler and breezy. How cold is the week’s one open question; the trend is colder.

High pressure settles overhead Saturday night and Sunday, and the wind dies. That sets up our first widespread frost, possible Saturday night or Sunday morning. Sunday remains cool.
